text: Web Access Builder: build a database app in your browser, and hand it out free.
Start by importing a Microsoft Access database. Tables keep their fields, data types and AutoNumber values, and queries are rebuilt from their original design.
Forms run as they were designed. This search form builds a filter in VBA and applies it to the list below.
PivotTable view is here too. Drag a field into the column area, and the totals follow.
The same layout drives a PivotChart. Change the chart type, and it redraws at once.
TreeView controls work too, with drag and drop, through the form's own code.
And VBA runs as VBA, in the browser. Set a breakpoint, click the button on the form, and the code pauses on that line. Step through, then carry on.
When it's ready, share it. Invite people by email, as a User who works with the data, or a Guest who only reads it.
They get the runtime: your forms and reports, and no design tools. Up to ten people use each database free.
Web Access Builder is in active development, and not yet for production use. Try the demo at webaccessbuilder.com.
